name: AMSites – Daily Problems
author: AM-Sites Web Experts

sections.description:
WordPress is brilliant at publishing, but every site owner sooner or later hits the same small, stubborn gaps: things WordPress simply leaves open. You end up with reminders in your calendar, manual late-night changes, extra plugins for every little job, or code snippets nobody remembers adding.

AMSites – Daily Problems closes those gaps. It is a growing toolbox of careful, practical solutions for everyday WordPress problems, collected in one lightweight plugin and one clear menu. Making WordPress Work Better, one real problem at a time.

Why Daily Problems

  • Real problems, not gimmicks. Every tool exists because site owners, editors and agencies run into that problem in daily work.
  • One plugin instead of many. Fewer plugins to update, fewer settings screens to learn, fewer conflicts.
  • It works like WordPress. The tools use the screens you already know: the editor sidebar, Quick Edit, Bulk Edit, the list of posts and pages.
  • Safe by default. Nothing changes on your site until you switch a tool on or set something up.

How it works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open the Daily Problems menu in your dashboard.
  3. Choose the tools you need. Everything is optional, and every tool starts with safe defaults.
  4. Use the tools where you already work: in the block editor or classic editor, in Quick Edit and Bulk Edit, or on the plugin’s own screens.

The tools work with posts, pages and custom post types, including custom post types that a theme or plugin adds later. You decide which post types are included.

The kinds of problems it solves

  • Scheduling and publishing: let content start, end and change at the right moment on its own, reliably and in your site’s timezone.
  • Visitor experience: decide what visitors see when content is not public, has ended or the site is being worked on, without broken pages or confusing redirects.
  • Content workflow: make everyday editing, reviewing and sharing faster and safer for editors, clients and teams.
  • Site care and safety: keep the site tidy and healthy, with clear records of what changed, careful limits and dry runs before anything is removed.

More tools are added over time. The plugin’s own screens always show the tools that are currently available.

Built for everyone

  • Site owners get features WordPress leaves out, without code.
  • Agencies get the same dependable toolbox on every client site.
  • Editors work in the screens they already know.
  • Developers get clean, standards-based code with documented filters and actions.
  • Page builder users can use the tools in the block editor, the classic editor, Elementor and, through a shortcode, almost any other builder.

Built with care

  • Security first: capability checks and nonces on every action, escaped output, sanitized input, and preview links that store only a hash of their secret.
  • Privacy: no external services, no tracking, no cookies for visitors, no data leaves your site.
  • Performance: scripts and styles load only on the screens that need them, and front-end work happens only when a tool is switched on.
  • Accessibility: labelled form fields, keyboard operable dialogs and screen reader text.
  • No ads, no upsells, no dashboard widgets.
  • Translation ready.

Compatibility

Daily Problems works with the block editor and the Classic Editor plugin, with block themes and classic themes, on single sites and multisite networks, and with WP-CLI. It includes dedicated support for Elementor, works with WooCommerce products, and clears the cache of common cache plugins such as WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache and WP Super Cache after scheduled changes. These are neutral compatibility notes; the plugin is not affiliated with these products.

External services

This plugin does not connect to any external service. It makes no remote requests, loads no external scripts, fonts or images, and sends no data anywhere.

Privacy

The plugin stores its data only in your own WordPress database: the user ID of the person behind each entry in its Activity Log, and the user ID of the creator of each client preview link (the link itself is stored only as a one-way hash). A short-lived counter of failed preview link attempts is kept under a one-way hash of the visitor’s IP address, never the address itself. The plugin adds a suggested paragraph to the privacy policy guide under Settings > Privacy.
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for “AMSites – Daily Problems”, then install and activate it. Alternatively upload the plugin zip under Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin, or upload the amsites-daily-problems folder to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it on the Plugins screen.
  2. Open Daily Problems in the admin menu.
  3. Review the Settings screen, choose the post types the tools should work with, and switch on the tools you need.
sections.faq:
Does it need WP-Cron? What if WP-Cron is disabled?

Scheduled changes use WordPress’s own scheduling (WP-Cron), with an exact event for each change plus a safety check every five minutes. If WP-Cron runs late or is disabled, overdue changes are also caught when someone visits the dashboard, and you can switch on an optional check on front-end visits. On sites that set DISABLE_WP_CRON, add a real server cron job that calls wp-cron.php (most hosts offer this) for changes to happen exactly on time. The Settings screen shows the WP-Cron status and has a “Run schedule check now” button.

How does it work with cache plugins?

After every scheduled change, the plugin clears the cache of the affected item (or the whole cache when the front page changes or maintenance mode is switched) in WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache and WP Super Cache, when one of them is active. Other caches can be cleared from the amsdp_after_cache_purge action, and the amsdp_purge_cache filter can prevent a purge.

Which post types are supported, and how do I exclude some?

Posts, pages and every custom post type that has an admin screen and public pages (for example WooCommerce products), including custom post types added later by a theme or plugin. Untick any post type under Daily Problems > Settings > Post types. Developers can also use the amsdp_post_types filter. Some tools that only make sense for pages, such as scheduling the front page, work with pages only.

Which timezone do scheduled times use?

Every date and time you enter is in your site’s timezone (Settings > General), and each scheduling field shows the current site time and timezone next to it. Times are stored internally in UTC, so a later timezone or daylight saving change does not move a schedule.

Does “Public Until” delete my content?

No. When the time is reached, the item is moved to Draft. Nothing is deleted, and you can publish it again at any time.

What do visitors see when an item has ended?

By default the normal “page not found” page of your theme. Per item, or for the whole site, you can instead redirect visitors to another address (301 or 302) or show a short “this has ended” message with HTTP status 410. Items you move to draft yourself always show the normal 404, and the plugin never redirects a hidden item to a similar address.

How does maintenance mode treat admins and search engines?

Logged-in users with the capability you choose (by default everyone who can edit posts) and visitors from IP addresses on your allow-list see the normal site, and the admin bar shows that maintenance mode is on. Everyone else, including search engines, receives HTTP status 503 with a Retry-After header, the standard way to tell search engines that the site is only temporarily unavailable, plus a noindex header so the maintenance page itself is never indexed. The dashboard, the login page and WP-Cron keep working. You can preview the maintenance page and schedule a start and end time.

How do client preview links work, and are they safe?

A preview link lets someone without a WordPress account view a draft, pending, scheduled or private item until the link expires (1 to 30 days) or you revoke it. The secret part of the link is created with a cryptographically secure random generator and is shown only once; the site stores only a hash of it. Invalid, expired or revoked links show a normal 404, repeated wrong attempts are throttled, and preview pages are sent with noindex, no-store and no-referrer headers so they are not indexed, cached or leaked to other sites.

How do scheduled updates work?

You create an update copy of a published item, edit the copy in peace, and choose when it should go live. At that time its content replaces the live content; the address, status and publish date stay the same, and the previous version is kept as a revision so you can restore it. The copy itself can never be published by accident. You can choose what happens when the live item was edited after the copy was made.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

Deactivating keeps all data and only stops the scheduled events. When you delete the plugin, all of its settings, schedules, log entries and scheduled events are removed only if “Delete data on uninstall” is switched on in Settings; otherwise everything is kept for a later reinstall. Your posts and pages are never deleted.

Is any data sent anywhere?

No. The plugin does not connect to any external service and sends no data off your site. See the Privacy section above for exactly what it stores locally.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. It can be activated per site or for the whole network. Each site has its own settings and schedules, and on uninstall each site’s data is removed according to that site’s own setting.

Does it work with page builders? What is the shortcode syntax?

Time-limited sections are available as a block in the block editor, as a toolbar button in the classic editor, and in Elementor as the “Time-limited Section (AMSites)” widget and as “Time-limited (AMSites)” controls in the Advanced tab of elements that support them. In any other builder, or anywhere shortcodes work, use:

[amsdp_show from="2030-12-01 09:00" until="2030-12-24 18:00" fallback="The offer has ended."]Your content[/amsdp_show]

Both dates use the site timezone and either one may be left out. Visitors see the content only inside the window; logged-in editors always see it, marked with an outline.

How do I report a problem?

Please open a topic in this plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org and include your WordPress, PHP and plugin versions and the steps to reproduce the problem. Please report security issues privately to the author through https://amsiteswebexperts.com/ instead of the public forum.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • First public release.
  • A toolbox for everyday WordPress problems in scheduling and publishing, visitor experience, content workflow and site care.
  • Works with posts, pages and custom post types, the block editor, the Classic Editor, Elementor (dedicated widget and Advanced tab controls) and any builder through a shortcode.
  • Security, privacy, performance and accessibility review against the WordPress plugin guidelines and coding standards.
